15.text: Maritime People, as stated before, took little part in the Taˊn˙ñɪn wars.

16.text: Tradition, however, mentions the dog-drivers now and then as joining the

17.text: reindeer-drivers; but the dog-drivers are always represented as of little account.

18.text: They come in at the end of the fighting, and are referred to in very few

19.text: words. Moreover, it seems that the dog-drivers were not Maritime settlers,

20.text: but only the poorest of the inland inhabitants, who, owing to lack of driving-

21.text: reindeer, travelled with dogs. In ancient times some of the inhabitants of the

22.text: interior were poor in reindeer, and so kept some dogs.

23.text: Eskimo Wars. — The wars of the Chukchee with the Eskimo are

24.text: preserved in the memory of the people with less distinctness, perhaps, because

25.text: they are more ancient. In some tales a cruel and implacable war between

26.text: two Maritime peoples is referred to. The one are described as the Chukchee;

27.text: the other, according to the details of their material life, must be the Eskimo.

28.text: They live by hunting seal, and have never seen a domesticated reindeer.
